sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀之制，神祇大享之外，每歲立春之日，祀青帝於東郊，帝宓羲配，勾芒、歲星、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: Under the Wude and Zhenguan regulations, apart from the great offerings to the spirits, on the day of Establishment of Spring each year the Green Emperor was sacrificed at the eastern suburb, with Emperor Fu Xi as associate, and Gou Mang, the Year Star, the Three Chronograms, and the Seven Lodgings attended the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude and Zhenguan rites, beyond great spirit offerings, each Establishment of Spring the Green Emperor was sacrificed at the eastern suburb with Fu Xi as associate and Gou Mang, the Year Star, the Three Chronograms, and Seven Lodgings in attendance.

sentences.zh: 立夏，祀赤帝於南郊，帝神農氏配，祝融、熒惑、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: At Establishment of Summer, the Red Emperor was sacrificed at the southern suburb, with Emperor Shen Nong as associate, and Zhu Rong, Sparkling Deluder, the Three Chronograms, and the Seven Lodgings attended.
translations.idiomatic: At Establishment of Summer: Red Emperor at the southern suburb, Shen Nong as associate, Zhu Rong, Sparkling Deluder, Three Chronograms, and Seven Lodgings attending.

sentences.zh: 季夏土王日，祀黃帝於南郊，帝軒轅配，後土、鎮星從祀。

translations.literal: On the earth-sovereign day of late summer, the Yellow Emperor was sacrificed at the southern suburb, with Emperor Xuan Yuan as associate, and Hou Tu and the Queller Star attended.
translations.idiomatic: Late-summer earth-sovereign day: Yellow Emperor at the southern suburb, Xuan Yuan as associate, Hou Tu and the Queller Star attending.

sentences.zh: 立秋，祀白帝於西郊，帝少昊配，蓐收、太白、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: At Establishment of Autumn, the White Emperor was sacrificed at the western suburb, with Emperor Shao Hao as associate, and Ru Shou, Great White, the Three Chronograms, and the Seven Lodgings attended.
translations.idiomatic: At Establishment of Autumn: White Emperor at the western suburb, Shao Hao as associate, Ru Shou, Great White, Three Chronograms, and Seven Lodgings attending.

sentences.zh: 立冬，祀黑帝於北郊，帝顓頊配，玄冥、辰星、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: At Establishment of Winter, the Black Emperor was sacrificed at the northern suburb, with Emperor Zhuan Xu as associate, and Xuan Ming, Chronogram Star, the Three Chronograms, and the Seven Lodgings attended.
translations.idiomatic: At Establishment of Winter: Black Emperor at the northern suburb, Zhuan Xu as associate, Xuan Ming, Chronogram Star, Three Chronograms, and Seven Lodgings attending.

sentences.zh: 每郊帝及配座，用方色犢各一，籩、豆各四，簠、簋各二，鉶、俎各一。

translations.literal: At each suburban sacrifice the emperor of the direction and the associate seat each used one calf of the direction's color, four platters and four beans, two grain tureens and two grain vessels, and one soup vessel and one cutting board.
translations.idiomatic: Each suburban rite: one direction-colored calf per direction-god and associate; four platters and beans, two tureens and vessels, one soup vessel and cutting board each.

sentences.zh: 勾芒已下五星及三辰、七宿，每宿牲用少牢，每座籩、豆、簠、簋、鉶、俎各一。

translations.literal: From Gou Mang down through the five stars and the Three Chronograms and Seven Lodgings, each lodging used a young bullock; each seat had one platter, bean, grain tureen, grain vessel, soup vessel, and cutting board.
translations.idiomatic: From Gou Mang through the five stars, Three Chronograms, and Seven Lodgings: young bullock per lodging; one full set of vessels per seat.

sentences.zh: 孟夏之月，龍星見，雩五方上帝於雩壇，五帝配於上，五官從祀於下。

translations.literal: In the first month of summer, when the Dragon Star appeared, rain prayer was made to the Five Directional High Gods at the rain altar; the Five Emperors were paired above and the Five Officials attended below.
translations.idiomatic: First summer month, Dragon Star visible: rain prayer to Five Directional High Gods at the rain altar; Five Emperors paired above, Five Officials below.

sentences.zh: 牲用方色犢十，籩豆已下，如郊祭之數。

translations.literal: Victims were ten direction-colored calves; platters, beans, and below followed the suburban sacrifice counts.
translations.idiomatic: Ten direction-colored calves; platters, beans, and the rest as at suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 帝嚳，祭於頓丘。

translations.literal: Emperor Ku was sacrificed at Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ku was sacrificed at Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 唐堯，契配，祭於平陽。

translations.literal: Tang Yao, with Qi as associate, was sacrificed at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, Qi paired, at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 虞舜，咎繇配，祭於河東。

translations.literal: Yu Shun, with Gao Yao as associate, was sacrificed at Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Shun, Gao Yao paired, at Hedong.

sentences.zh: 夏禹，伯益配，祭于安邑。

translations.literal: Yu of Xia, with Bo Yi as associate, was sacrificed at Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia, Bo Yi paired, at Anyi.

sentences.zh: 殷湯，伊尹配，祭于偃師。

translations.literal: Tang of Yin, with Yi Yin as associate, was sacrificed at Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang of Yin, Yi Yin paired, at Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 周文王，太公配，祭於邦。

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou, with Grand Duke as associate, was sacrificed at Bang.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen, Grand Duke paired, at Bang.

sentences.zh: 周武王、周公、召公配，祭於鎬。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou, with Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao as associates, was sacrificed at Hao.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu, Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao paired, at Hao.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖，蕭何配，祭於長陵。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu, with Xiao He as associate, was sacrificed at Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, Xiao He paired, at Changling.

sentences.zh: 三年一祭，以仲春之月。

translations.literal: Sacrifice once every three years, in the mid-spring month.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years, mid-spring.

sentences.zh: 牲皆用太牢。

translations.literal: All victims used the great offering.
translations.idiomatic: All victims: great offering.

sentences.zh: 祀官以當界州長官，有故，遣上佐行事。

translations.literal: Sacrificing officers were the prefectural chief of the relevant circuit; if prevented, a senior aide was sent to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit prefect sacrificed; if absent, a senior aide performed.

sentences.zh: 五嶽、四鎮、四海、四瀆，年別一祭，各以五郊迎氣日祭之。

translations.literal: The Five Marchmounts, Four Garrisons, Four Seas, and Four Watercourses each had one sacrifice per year, each on the day of receiving qi at the five suburban altars.
translations.idiomatic: Five Marchmounts, Four Garrisons, Four Seas, and Four Watercourses: annual sacrifice on each direction's suburban qi-receiving day.

sentences.zh: 東嶽岱山，祭於祇州；

translations.literal: Eastern Marchmount Mount Dai was sacrificed at Qizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Marchmount Dai at Qizhou;

sentences.zh: 東鎮沂山，祭於沂州；

translations.literal: Eastern Garrison Mount Yi at Yizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Garrison Yi at Yizhou;

sentences.zh: 東海，於萊州；

translations.literal: Eastern Sea at Laizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Sea: Laizhou;

sentences.zh: 東瀆大淮，于唐州。

translations.literal: Eastern Watercourse the Great Huai at Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Watercourse Great Huai at Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 南嶽衡山，於衡州；

translations.literal: Southern Marchmount Mount Heng at Hengzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Marchmount Heng at Hengzhou;

sentences.zh: 南鎮會稽，於越州；

translations.literal: Southern Garrison Kuaiji at Yuezhou;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Garrison: Kuaiji at Yuezhou;

sentences.zh: 南海，于廣州；

translations.literal: Southern Sea at Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Sea: Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 南瀆大江，於益州。

translations.literal: Southern Watercourse the Great Jiang at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Watercourse Great Jiang at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 中嶽嵩山，於洛州。

translations.literal: Central Marchmount Mount Song at Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Central Marchmount Song at Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 西嶽華山，于華州；

translations.literal: Western Marchmount Mount Hua at Huazhou;
translations.idiomatic: Western Marchmount Hua at Huazhou;

sentences.zh: 西鎮吳山，於隴州；

translations.literal: Western Garrison Mount Wu at Longzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Western Garrison Wu at Longzhou;

sentences.zh: 西海、西瀆大河，於同州。

translations.literal: Western Sea and Western Watercourse the Great He at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Western Sea and Western Watercourse Great He at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 北嶽恆山，於定州；

translations.literal: Northern Marchmount Mount Heng at Dingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Marchmount Heng at Dingzhou;

sentences.zh: 北鎮醫無閭山，于營州；

translations.literal: Northern Garrison Mount Yiwulü at Yingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Garrison Yiwulü at Yingzhou;

sentences.zh: 北海、北瀆大濟，於洛州。

translations.literal: Northern Sea and Northern Watercourse the Great Ji at Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Sea and Northern Watercourse Great Ji at Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 其牲皆用太牢，籩、豆各四。

translations.literal: All victims used the great offering; four platters and four beans each.
translations.idiomatic: Victims: great offering; four platters and four beans each.

sentences.zh: 祀官以當界都督刺史充。

translations.literal: Sacrificing officers were filled by the area's military commissioner and prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Area military commissioner and prefect sacrificed.

sentences.zh: 仲春、仲秋二時戊日，祭太社、太稷，社以勾龍配，稷以後稷配。

translations.literal: On the wu days of mid-spring and mid-autumn, Great Soil Mound and Great Grain Mound were sacrificed; Soil Mound had Gou Long as associate, Grain Mound Hou Ji as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring and mid-autumn wu days: Great Soil and Great Grain; Gou Long paired with Soil, Hou Ji with Grain.

sentences.zh: 社、稷各用太牢一，牲色並黑，籩、豆、簠、簋各二，鉶、俎各三。

translations.literal: Soil Mound and Grain Mound each used one great offering; victims were all black; two platters, beans, grain tureens, and vessels each; three soup vessels and cutting boards each.
translations.idiomatic: Each mound: one great offering, black victims, two platters, beans, tureens, vessels, three soup vessels and cutting boards.

sentences.zh: 春分，朝日于國城之東；

translations.literal: At the spring equinox, the sun was greeted at the east of the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Spring equinox: greet the sun east of the capital;

sentences.zh: 秋分，夕月于國城之西。

translations.literal: at the autumn equinox, the moon was seen off at the west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: autumn equinox: see off the moon west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 各用方色犢一，籩、豆各四，簠、簋、鉶、俎各一。

translations.literal: Each used one calf of the direction's color, four platters and four beans, and one grain tureen, grain vessel, soup vessel, and cutting board.
translations.idiomatic: Each: one direction-colored calf, four platters and beans, one each of tureen, vessel, soup vessel, and cutting board.

sentences.zh: 孟春吉亥，祭帝社于藉田，天子親耕；

translations.literal: On an auspicious hai day in early spring, the emperor's soil mound was sacrificed at the sacred field and the Son of Heaven plowed in person;
translations.idiomatic: Early-spring auspicious hai: emperor's soil mound at the sacred field; the Son of Heaven plowed.

sentences.zh: 季春吉巳，祭先蠶于公桑，皇后親桑。

translations.literal: on an auspicious si day in late spring, the First Silkworm was sacrificed at the public mulberry grove and the empress reeled silk in person.
translations.idiomatic: Late-spring auspicious si: First Silkworm at the public mulberry; the empress reeled silk.

sentences.zh: 並用太牢，籩、豆各九。

translations.literal: Both used the great offering; nine platters and nine beans each.
translations.idiomatic: Both: great offering; nine platters and nine beans.

sentences.zh: 將蠶日，內侍省預奉移所司所事。

translations.literal: On the day before silkworm rites, the Palace Domestic Service pre-delivered orders to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Eve of silkworm rites: Palace Domestic Service notified the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 諸祭祀卜日，皆先卜上旬；

translations.literal: For all sacrifices the day was divined, always first in the first ten-day period;
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice days: divined, upper ten-day period first;

sentences.zh: 不吉，次卜中旬、下旬。

translations.literal: if inauspicious, then the middle and lower periods.
translations.idiomatic: if inauspicious, then middle and lower periods.

sentences.zh: 筮日亦如之。

translations.literal: Day by stalk-casting followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Stalk-casting for days followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 其先蠶一祭，節氣若晚，即於節氣後取日。

translations.literal: For the First Silkworm sacrifice alone, if the solar term came late, the day was taken after the term.
translations.idiomatic: First Silkworm alone: if the term ran late, the day followed the term.

sentences.zh: 立春後醜，祀風師于國城東北；

translations.literal: After Establishment of Spring on a chou day, the Wind Master was sacrificed northeast of the capital;
translations.idiomatic: After Establishment of Spring, chou day: Wind Master northeast of the capital;

sentences.zh: 立夏後申，祀雨師于國城西南；

translations.literal: after Establishment of Summer on a shen day, the Rain Master southwest of the capital;
translations.idiomatic: after Establishment of Summer, shen day: Rain Master southwest;

sentences.zh: 立秋後辰，祀靈星于國城東南；

translations.literal: after Establishment of Autumn on a chen day, the Spirit Star southeast of the capital;
translations.idiomatic: after Establishment of Autumn, chen day: Spirit Star southeast;

sentences.zh: 立冬後亥，祀司中、司命、司人、司祿于國城西北。

translations.literal: after Establishment of Winter on a hai day, Director of the Center, Director of Fate, Director of the People, and Director of Emolument northwest of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: after Establishment of Winter, hai day: Director of Center, Fate, People, and Emolument northwest.

sentences.zh: 各用羊一，籩、豆各二，簠、簋各一。

translations.literal: Each used one sheep, two platters and two beans, and one grain tureen and grain vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Each: one sheep, two platters and beans, one tureen and vessel.

sentences.zh: 季冬晦，堂贈儺，磔牲于宮門及城四門，各用雄雞一。

translations.literal: On the last day of late winter, hall presentation and exorcism; victims were dismembered at the palace gate and the four city gates, each place one cock.
translations.idiomatic: Late-winter last day: hall presentation and exorcism; victims dismembered at palace gate and four city gates, one cock each.

sentences.zh: 仲春，祭馬祖；

translations.literal: In mid-spring, the Horse Ancestor was sacrificed;
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring: Horse Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 仲夏，祭先牧；

translations.literal: in mid-summer, the First Herdsman;
translations.idiomatic: mid-summer: First Herdsman;

sentences.zh: 仲秋，祭馬社；

translations.literal: in mid-autumn, the Horse Soil Mound;
translations.idiomatic: mid-autumn: Horse Soil Mound;

sentences.zh: 仲冬，祭馬步。

translations.literal: in mid-winter, the Horse Pace.
translations.idiomatic: mid-winter: Horse Pace.

sentences.zh: 並於大澤，用剛日。

translations.literal: All were at the Great Marsh on a yang day.
translations.idiomatic: All at the Great Marsh on a yang day.

sentences.zh: 牲各用羊一，籩、豆各二，簠、簋各一。

translations.literal: Each victim was one sheep; two platters and two beans, one grain tureen and grain vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Each: one sheep, two platters and beans, one tureen and vessel.

sentences.zh: 季冬藏冰，仲春開冰，並用黑牡、秬黍，祭司寒之神於冰室，籩、豆各二，簠、簋、俎各一。

translations.literal: Late winter stored ice; mid-spring opened ice; both used black bull and glutinous millet; the Cold Chamber spirit was sacrificed at the ice house—two platters and two beans, one grain tureen, grain vessel, and cutting board.
translations.idiomatic: Late winter ice stored, mid-spring opened: black bull and glutinous millet; Cold Chamber spirit at the ice house; two platters and beans, one tureen, vessel, and cutting board.

sentences.zh: 其開冰，加以桃弧棘矢，設於神座。

translations.literal: When opening ice, peach bow and thorn arrows were added and set at the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Ice opening added peach bow and thorn arrows at the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 季冬寅日，蠟祭百神於南郊。

translations.literal: On a yin day in late winter, wax sacrifice to the hundred spirits at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Late-winter yin day: wax sacrifice to hundred spirits at southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 大明、夜明，用犢二，籩、豆各四，簠、簋、鉶、俎各一。

translations.literal: Great Brightness and Night Brightness each used two calves, four platters and four beans, and one grain tureen, grain vessel, soup vessel, and cutting board.
translations.idiomatic: Great Brightness and Night Brightness: two calves each, four platters and beans, one full vessel set each.

sentences.zh: 神農氏及伊耆氏，各用少牢一，籩、豆各四，簠、簋、鉶、俎各一。

translations.literal: Shen Nong and Yi Qi each used one young bullock, four platters and four beans, and one grain tureen, grain vessel, soup vessel, and cutting board.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Nong and Yi Qi: young bullock each, four platters and beans, one full vessel set each.

sentences.zh: 後稷及五方、十二次、五官、五方田畯、五嶽、四鎮、四海、四瀆以下，方別各用少牢一，當方不熟者則闕之。

translations.literal: Hou Ji and the Five Directions, twelve chronograms, five officials, five directional field masters, Five Marchmounts, Four Garrisons, Four Seas, Four Watercourses and below—each direction one young bullock; where the direction's harvest failed, that rite was omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji, Five Directions, twelve chronograms, five officials, field masters, marchmounts, garrisons, seas, watercourses and below: one young bullock per direction; failed harvest omitted that rite.

sentences.zh: 其日祭井泉於川澤之下，用羊一。

translations.literal: That day wells and springs were sacrificed below streams and marshes, using one sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Same day: wells and springs below streams and marshes, one sheep.

sentences.zh: 卯日祭社稷于社宮，辰日臘享於太廟，用牲皆準時祭。

translations.literal: On mao day soil and grain mounds were sacrificed at the mound shrine; on chen day la offering at the Grand Temple; victims all followed seasonal sacrifice standards.
translations.idiomatic: Mao day: soil and grain at mound shrine; chen day: la at Grand Temple; victims per seasonal standard.

sentences.zh: 井泉用羊二。

translations.literal: Wells and springs used two sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Wells and springs: two sheep.

sentences.zh: 二十八宿，五方之山林、川澤，五方之丘陵、墳衍、原隰，五方之鱗、羽、臝、毛、介，五方之水墉、坊、郵表畷，五方之貓、於菟及龍、麟、硃鳥、白虎、玄武，方別各用少牢一，各座籩、豆、簠、簋、俎各一。

translations.literal: The twenty-eight lodgings, five directional mountains and forests and streams and marshes, five directional hills and mounds and banks and plains, five directional scale, feather, naked, fur, and shell creatures, five directional water walls, dykes, beacon mounds, and boundary markers, five directional cats, wutu, dragon, qilin, vermilion bird, white tiger, and dark warrior—each direction one young bullock; each seat one platter, bean, grain tureen, grain vessel, and cutting board.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eight lodgings, directional mountains, waters, hills, creatures, walls, cats, wutu, dragon, qilin, vermilion bird, white tiger, dark warrior: young bullock and one vessel set per direction per seat.

sentences.zh: 蠟祭凡一百八十七座。

translations.literal: Wax sacrifice in all comprised one hundred eighty-seven seats.
translations.idiomatic: Wax sacrifice: one hundred eighty-seven seats in all.

sentences.zh: 當方年穀不登，則闕其祀。

translations.literal: If the year's grain in a direction did not mature, that direction's rite was omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Failed harvest in a direction: omit that rite.

sentences.zh: 蠟祭之日，祭五方井泉於山澤之下，用羊一，籩、豆各二，簠、簋、及俎各一。

translations.literal: On wax day the five directional wells and springs were sacrificed below mountains and marshes, one sheep, two platters and two beans, one grain tureen, grain vessel, and cutting board.
translations.idiomatic: Wax day: five directional wells and springs below mountains and marshes; one sheep, two platters and beans, one tureen, vessel, and cutting board.

sentences.zh: 蠟之明日，又祭社稷于社宮，如春秋二仲之禮。

translations.literal: The day after wax, soil and grain mounds were again sacrificed at the mound shrine, as in the mid-spring and mid-autumn rites.
translations.idiomatic: Day after wax: soil and grain at mound shrine, as in mid-spring and mid-autumn.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，更定籩、豆之數，始一例。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era the counts of platters and beans were revised and first unified.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqing: platter and bean counts revised and unified.

sentences.zh: 大祀籩、豆各十二，中祀各十，小祀各八。

translations.literal: Great sacrifice: twelve platters and twelve beans; middle sacrifice ten each; small sacrifice eight each.
translations.idiomatic: Great: twelve platters and beans; middle: ten; small: eight.

sentences.zh: 京師孟夏以後旱，則祈雨，審理冤獄，賑恤窮乏，掩骼埋胔。

translations.literal: After mid-summer in the capital, if drought came, rain was prayed for, wrongful cases reviewed, the destitute relieved, and exposed bones buried.
translations.idiomatic: Capital after mid-summer drought: pray rain, review cases, relieve the poor, bury exposed dead.

sentences.zh: 先祈嶽鎮、海瀆及諸山川能出雲雨，皆於北郊望而告之。

translations.literal: First prayer was to marchmounts, garrisons, seas, watercourses, and mountains and rivers that could send rain clouds—all greeted and announced at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: First: marchmounts, garrisons, seas, watercourses, and rain-bearing rivers, greeted and announced at northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 又祈社稷，又祈宗廟，每七日皆一祈。

translations.literal: Then soil and grain mounds, then the ancestral temple—each every seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Then soil and grain, then ancestral temple—each every seven days.

sentences.zh: 不雨，還從嶽瀆。

translations.literal: If no rain, return to marchmounts and watercourses.
translations.idiomatic: No rain: return to marchmounts and watercourses.

sentences.zh: 旱甚，則大雩，秋分後不雩。

translations.literal: If drought was extreme, great rain prayer; no great prayer after autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Extreme drought: great rain prayer; none after autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 初祈後一旬不雨，即徙市，禁屠殺，斷傘扇，造土龍。

translations.literal: After the first prayer, if ten days passed without rain, the market was moved, slaughter forbidden, umbrellas and fans barred, and an earthen dragon made.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after first prayer without rain: move the market, ban slaughter, umbrellas, and fans; make an earthen dragon.

sentences.zh: 雨足，則報祀。

translations.literal: When rain sufficed, thanksgiving sacrifice was offered.
translations.idiomatic: Rain enough: thanksgiving sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祈用酒醢，報准常祀，皆有司行事。

translations.literal: Prayer used wine and dried meat; thanksgiving followed regular sacrifice; all performed by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer: wine and dried meat; thanksgiving: regular standard; relevant offices performed.

sentences.zh: 已齊未祈而雨，及所經祈者，皆報祀。

translations.literal: If rain came after fasting but before prayer, or at any place already prayed, thanksgiving was still offered.
translations.idiomatic: Rain after fasting before prayer, or at any prayed site: still offer thanksgiving.

sentences.zh: 若霖雨不已，禜京城諸門，門別三日，每日一禜。

translations.literal: If heavy rain did not cease, supplication was made at the capital gates, three days per gate, one supplication daily.
translations.idiomatic: Unending heavy rain: supplication at capital gates, three days per gate, once daily.

sentences.zh: 不止，乃祈山川、嶽鎮、海瀆；

translations.literal: If it did not stop, mountains, rivers, marchmounts, garrisons, seas, and watercourses were prayed;
translations.idiomatic: If unceasing: pray mountains, rivers, marchmounts, garrisons, seas, watercourses;

sentences.zh: 三日不止，祈社稷、宗廟。

translations.literal: after three days without stopping, soil and grain mounds and the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: three days more without stopping: soil and grain and ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 其州縣，禜城門；

translations.literal: In prefectures and counties, city gates were supplicated;
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties: supplicate city gates;

sentences.zh: 不止，祈界內山川及社稷。

translations.literal: if unceasing, mountains and rivers within the circuit and soil and grain mounds.
translations.idiomatic: if unceasing: circuit mountains and rivers and soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 三禜、一祈，皆准京式，並用酒脯醢。

translations.literal: Three supplications and one prayer all followed the capital pattern, all using wine, dried flesh, and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: Three supplications and one prayer: capital pattern; wine, dried flesh, and dried meat.

sentences.zh: 國城門報用少牢，州縣城門用一特牲。

translations.literal: Capital gates used young bullock for thanksgiving; prefectural and county gates one special victim.
translations.idiomatic: Capital gate thanksgiving: young bullock; prefectural and county gates: one special victim.

sentences.zh: 太宗貞觀三年正月，親祭先農，躬禦耒耜，藉於千畝之甸。

translations.literal: In the first month of Zhenguan 3, Taizong personally sacrificed to the First Farmer, took the plow in hand, and plowed the thousand-mu field.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 3, first month: Taizong sacrificed to First Farmer, took the plow, plowed the thousand-mu field.

sentences.zh: 初，晉時南遷，後魏來自雲、朔，中原分裂，又雜以犬熏戎，代曆周、隋，此禮久廢，而今始行之，觀者莫不駭躍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jin moved south and Northern Wei came from Yun and Shuo, the central plains were divided and mixed with dog-and-deer Rong; through Zhou and Sui dynasties this rite had long been abandoned, and now it was performed for the first time—onlookers were all astonished and exultant.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's southward move and Wei from Yun and Shuo, the plains split and mixed with Rong; through Zhou and Sui the rite had lapsed—now revived, onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 於是秘書郎岑文本獻《藉田頌》以美之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Secretariat Gentleman Cen Wende presented the "Sacred Field Eulogy" to praise it.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Cen Wende then offered the "Sacred Field Eulogy" in praise.

sentences.zh: 初，議藉田方面所在，給事中孔穎達曰：「禮，天子藉田于南郊，諸侯于東郊。

translations.literal: Earlier, when debating where the sacred-field plowing should face, Remonstrator Kong Yingda said: "The Rites state that the Son of Heaven plows the sacred field at the southern suburb and feudal lords at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: When debating sacred-field orientation, Remonstrator Kong Yingda said: "Rites place the Son of Heaven's sacred field at the southern suburb and lords' at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝猶于東南。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin still used the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wudi still plowed toward the southeast.

sentences.zh: 今於城東置壇，不合古禮。

translations.literal: Now an altar is set east of the city, which does not accord with ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: An altar east of the city does not match ancient rites.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「禮緣人情，亦何常之有。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Taizong said: "Rites follow human feeling—what is ever constant?
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Taizong said: "Rites follow feeling—what is ever constant?

sentences.zh: 且《虞書》雲'平秩東作'，則是堯、舜敬授人時，已在東矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Documents of Yu says "order the work of the east"—thus Yao and Shun in granting the seasons were already in the east.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Yu says "order the work of the east"—Yao and Shun granting seasons were already in the east.

sentences.zh: 又乘青輅、推黛耜者，所以順於春氣，故知合在東方。

translations.literal: Again, riding the green carriage and pushing the dark plow is to accord with spring qi; thus one knows it should be in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Green carriage and dark plow accord with spring qi—so it belongs in the east.

sentences.zh: 且朕見居少陽之地，田于東郊，蓋其宜矣」於是遂定。

translations.literal: Moreover I now dwell in the place of Lesser Yang; to plow at the eastern suburb is surely fitting. The passage concluded." Thereupon it was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: I dwell in Lesser Yang; eastern-suburb plowing is fitting. The quote ended. It was fixed.

sentences.zh: 自後每歲常令有司行事。

translations.literal: Afterward each year the relevant offices were routinely ordered to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the relevant offices performed it yearly.

sentences.zh: 則天時，改藉田壇為先農。

translations.literal: In the Wu Zetian era the sacred-field altar was changed to First Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian era: sacred-field altar renamed First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，禮部尚書祝欽明與禮官等奏曰：「謹按經典，無先農之文。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming and ritual officers memorialized: "We have examined the classics and find no text on First Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: Shenlong 1: Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming and ritual officers memorialized: "Classics contain no First Farmer text.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·祭法》云：'王自為立社，曰王社。

translations.literal: The "Regulations of Sacrifice" in the Book of Rites says: 'When the king establishes a mound for himself, it is called the king's mound.'
translations.idiomatic: Book of Rites "Regulations of Sacrifice": when the king establishes a mound for himself, it is the king's mound.

sentences.zh: '先儒以為社在藉田，《詩》之《載芟篇序》雲'春藉田而祈社稷'是也。

translations.literal: Former scholars held that the mound was at the sacred field; the preface to the Odes' "Zai Yan" says "spring sacred-field plowing and prayer to soil and grain mounds"—that is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Former scholars placed the mound at the sacred field; the "Zai Yan" preface says "spring sacred-field plowing and prayer to soil and grain"—that meaning.

sentences.zh: 永徽年中猶名藉田，垂拱已後刪定，改為先農。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era it was still called sacred-field plowing; after Chuigong it was revised and changed to First Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghui: still sacred-field plowing; after Chuigong revised to First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 先農與社，本是一神，頻有改張，以惑人聽。

translations.literal: First Farmer and the mound were originally one spirit; frequent changes confused listeners.
translations.idiomatic: First Farmer and the mound were one spirit; repeated changes confused people.

sentences.zh: 其先農壇請改為帝社壇，以應禮經王社之義。

translations.literal: The First Farmer altar should be changed to the Emperor's Soil Mound altar to answer the canonical meaning of the king's mound.
translations.idiomatic: Change the First Farmer altar to Emperor's Soil Mound altar per the king's mound in canon.

sentences.zh: 其祭先農既改為帝社壇，仍准令用孟春吉亥祠後土，以勾龍氏配。

translations.literal: Since First Farmer sacrifice is changed to Emperor's Soil Mound altar, still follow the statute using an auspicious hai day in early spring to sacrifice to Hou Tu, with Gou Long as associate.
translations.idiomatic: With First Farmer changed to Emperor's Soil Mound altar, still sacrifice Hou Tu on early-spring auspicious hai with Gou Long paired.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Approved.

sentences.zh: 於是改先農為帝社壇，於壇西立帝稷壇，禮同太社、太稷，其壇不備方色，所以異於太社也。

translations.literal: Thereupon First Farmer was changed to Emperor's Soil Mound altar; west of the altar Emperor's Grain Mound altar was set up—rites like Great Soil and Great Grain; the altar lacked directional colors to distinguish it from Great Soil.
translations.idiomatic: First Farmer became Emperor's Soil Mound altar; Emperor's Grain Mound west of it—rites like Great Soil and Grain, without directional colors unlike Great Soil.

sentences.zh: 睿宗太極元年，親祀先農，躬耕帝藉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Supreme Ultimate, Ruizong personally sacrificed to First Farmer and plowed the emperor's sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Ultimate 1: Ruizong sacrificed to First Farmer and plowed the emperor's field.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: When rites ended, a great amnesty and era change.
translations.idiomatic: Rites ended: great amnesty and era change.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元二十二年冬，禮部員外郎王仲丘又上疏請行藉田之禮。

translations.literal: In winter of Kaiyuan 22, Ritual Department Vice Director Wang Zhongqiu again memorialized to perform sacred-field rites.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 22 winter: Ritual Vice Director Wang Zhongqiu again asked for sacred-field rites.

sentences.zh: 二十三年正月，親祀神農於東郊，以勾芒配。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-third year, Shen Nong was personally sacrificed at the eastern suburb with Gou Mang as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Year 23, first month: Shen Nong at eastern suburb, Gou Mang paired.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，躬禦耒耜於千畝之甸。

translations.literal: When rites ended, he took the plow in hand at the thousand-mu field.
translations.idiomatic: Rites ended: he took the plow at the thousand-mu field.

sentences.zh: 時有司進儀注：「天子三推，公卿九推，庶人終畝。

translations.literal: At the time the relevant offices presented ritual notes: "The Son of Heaven three pushes, nobles and ministers nine pushes, commoners finish the mu.
translations.idiomatic: Relevant offices presented notes: Son of Heaven three pushes, nobles nine, commoners finish the mu.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗欲重勸耕藉，遂進耕五十余步，盡壟乃止。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Xuanzong wished to stress plowing encouragement and advanced fifty-odd steps in plowing, stopping only at the end of the ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Xuanzong stressed plowing encouragement, advanced fifty-odd steps, and stopped at the ridge end.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，輦還齋宮，大赦。

translations.literal: When rites ended, the carriage returned to the fast palace and a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Rites ended: return to fast palace, great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 侍耕、執牛官皆等級賜帛。

translations.literal: Officials who attended plowing and held the ox were all rewarded with silk by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Plowing attendants and ox handlers received silk by rank.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元二十六年，又親往東郊迎氣，祀青帝，以勾芒配，歲星及三辰七宿從祀。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 26 Xuanzong again personally went to the eastern suburb to receive qi and sacrificed to the Green Emperor with Gou Mang as associate; the Year Star and Three Chronograms and Seven Lodgings attended.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 26: Xuanzong received qi at eastern suburb, sacrificed to Green Emperor with Gou Mang, Year Star, Three Chronograms, and Seven Lodgings attending.

sentences.zh: 其壇本在春明門外，玄宗以祀所隘狹，始移于滻水之東面，而值望春宮。

translations.literal: The altar had originally been outside Spring Bright Gate; Xuanzong found the sacrifice site cramped and first moved it east of the Chan River, facing Wangchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The altar had been outside Spring Bright Gate; Xuanzong moved it east of the Chan facing Wangchun Palace as cramped.

sentences.zh: 其壇一成，壇上及四面皆青色。

translations.literal: The altar had one tier; the altar top and four sides were all green.
translations.idiomatic: One-tier altar; top and four sides green.

sentences.zh: 勾芒壇在東南。

translations.literal: Gou Mang's altar was southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Mang's altar: southeast.

sentences.zh: 歲星已下各為一小壇，在青壇之北。

translations.literal: From the Year Star down each had a small altar north of the green altar.
translations.idiomatic: Year Star and below: small altars north of the green altar.

sentences.zh: 親祀之時，有瑞雪，壇下侍臣及百僚拜賀稱慶。

translations.literal: At personal sacrifice auspicious snow fell; attendants below the altar and the hundred officials bowed in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Personal sacrifice: auspicious snow; attendants and officials below bowed in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 肅宗乾元二年春正月丁丑，將有事於九宮之神，兼行藉田禮。

translations.literal: In the first month of Qianyuan 2, on dingchou, rites were to be held for the Nine Palaces spirits and sacred-field rites were also performed.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan 2, first month dingchou: Nine Palaces spirits and sacred-field rites together.

sentences.zh: 自明鳳門出，至通化門，釋軷而入壇，行宿齋于宮。

translations.literal: Exiting Bright Phoenix Gate to Tonghua Gate, the shaft-horse rite was released and entry made to the altar; lodging fast was kept in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Out Bright Phoenix Gate to Tonghua Gate, shaft-horse rite, into altar, fast in palace.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，禮畢，將耕藉，先至於先農之壇。

translations.literal: On wuyin rites ended; about to plow the sacred field, he first went to the First Farmer altar.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyin: rites ended; before sacred-field plowing, first to First Farmer altar.

sentences.zh: 因閱耒耜，有雕刻文飾，謂左右曰：「田器，農人執之，在於樸素，豈文飾乎？

translations.literal: Inspecting the plow, he found carved ornament and said to attendants: "Field tools are held by farmers and should be plain—how ornament?
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the plow he found carving and asked attendants why farm tools should bear ornament.

sentences.zh: 」乃命徹之。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." He ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. He ordered them removed.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「古之帝王，臨禦天下，莫不務農敦本，保儉為先，蓋用勤身率下也。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Ancient emperors overseeing the realm all stressed agriculture and honored the root, keeping frugality first—thereby personally urging those below.
translations.idiomatic: Edict: "Ancient emperors all stressed agriculture, honored the root, and kept frugality—personally urging those below.

sentences.zh: 屬東耕啟候，爰事藉田，將欲勸彼蒸人，所以執茲耒耜。

translations.literal: Now as eastern plowing opens the season, sacred-field affairs begin, wishing to encourage the common people—thus holding this plow.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern plowing opens the season; sacred-field work begins to encourage the people—thus this plow.

sentences.zh: 如聞有司所造農器，妄加雕飾，殊匪典章。

translations.literal: We hear the relevant offices' farm tools were recklessly carved and ornamented, greatly violating statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Relevant offices' farm tools were recklessly carved—greatly violating statutes.

sentences.zh: 況紺轅縹軏，固前王有制，崇奢尚靡，諒為政所疵。

translations.literal: Moreover dark shafts and light axles—former kings had fixed rules; exalting luxury violates governance.
translations.idiomatic: Dark shafts and light axles had fixed rules; exalting luxury flaws governance.

sentences.zh: 靖言思之，良用歎息，豈朕法堯舜、重茅茨之意耶！

translations.literal: Reflecting on this, we sigh deeply—how is this my intent to emulate Yao and Shun and value thatched roofs!
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting, we sigh—how is this emulating Yao and Shun and valuing thatched roofs!

sentences.zh: 其所造雕飾者宜停。

translations.literal: Carved and ornamented ones should cease.
translations.idiomatic: Carved ornamentation should cease.

sentences.zh: 仍令有司依農用常式，即別改造，庶萬方黎庶，知朕意焉。

translations.literal: Still order the relevant offices to follow ordinary farm patterns and remake them separately, so the myriad people may know our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Order relevant offices to follow ordinary farm patterns and remake them so the people know our intent.

sentences.zh: 」翌日己卯，致祭神農氏，以後稷配享。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Next day jimao: sacrifice to Shen Nong with Hou Ji as joint offering.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Next day jimao: Shen Nong with Hou Ji joint offering.

sentences.zh: 肅宗冕而硃紘，躬秉耒耜而九推焉。

translations.literal: Suzong wore cap and vermilion knee-guards, personally held the plow and performed nine pushes.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong capped and vermilion knee-guards, held the plow, nine pushes.

sentences.zh: 禮官奏陛下合三推，今過禮。

translations.literal: Ritual officers memorialized that Your Majesty should perform three pushes; now it exceeds rite.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers: Your Majesty should three-push; now exceeds rite.

sentences.zh: 肅宗曰：「朕以身率下，自當過之，恨不能終於千畝耳。

translations.literal: Suzong said: "I personally lead those below and should exceed it—I regret not finishing the thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong said he leads from the front and should exceed it—he regrets not finishing the thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 」既而佇立久之，觀公卿、諸侯、王公已下耕畢。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." He then stood long, watching nobles, feudal lords, and imperial princes and below finish plowing.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. He stood long watching nobles, lords, and princes finish plowing.

sentences.zh: 太宗貞觀十四年春正月庚子，命有司讀春令，詔百官之長，升太極殿列坐面聽之。

translations.literal: In the first month of Zhenguan 14, on gengzi, the relevant offices were ordered to read the spring ordinance; an edict had the heads of the hundred offices ascend the Supreme Ultimate Hall and sit in rows facing inward to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 14, first month gengzi: read spring ordinance; hundred-office heads sat at Supreme Ultimate Hall to listen.

sentences.zh: 開元二十六年，玄宗命太常卿韋絛每月進《月令》一篇。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 26 Xuanzong ordered Director of Ritual Wei Tiao each month to present one section of the Monthly Ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 26: Director of Ritual Wei Tiao monthly presented one Monthly Ordinances section.

sentences.zh: 是後每孟月視日，玄宗禦宣政殿，側置一榻，東面置案，命韋絛坐而讀之。

translations.literal: Thereafter on each early-month audience day Xuanzong attended Xuanzheng Hall; a couch was set to the side, a desk to the east, and Wei Tiao was ordered to sit and read.
translations.idiomatic: Each early-month audience: Xuanzong at Xuanzheng Hall, side couch, east desk, Wei Tiao seated reading.

sentences.zh: 諸司官長，亦升殿列座而聽焉。

translations.literal: Heads of the various offices also ascended the hall and sat in rows to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Office heads also ascended and listened in rows.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，罷之。

translations.literal: After more than a year it was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: After a year plus it ceased.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年十二月丙寅立春，肅宗禦宣政殿，命太常卿於休烈讀春令。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month of Qianyuan 1, bingyin, Establishment of Spring; Suzong attended Xuanzheng Hall and ordered Director of Ritual Yu Xiulie to read the spring ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan 1, twelfth month bingyin new moon, Establishment of Spring: Suzong at Xuanzheng Hall, Yu Xiulie read spring ordinance.

sentences.zh: 常參官五品已上正員，並升殿預坐而聽之。

translations.literal: Regular-attendance officials of fifth rank and above in substantive posts all ascended the hall and sat beforehand to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Regular fifth-rank and above substantive officials ascended and listened.

sentences.zh: 舊儀，嶽瀆已下，祝版禦署訖，北面再拜。

translations.literal: Former practice: for marchmounts and watercourses and below, after the prayer board was imperially signed, one bowed facing north twice.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly: marchmounts and watercourses below—after imperial signature on prayer board, bow north twice.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年，有司上言曰：「伏以天子父天而母地，兄日而姊月，于禮應敬，故有再拜之儀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengsheng, the relevant offices memorialized: "We consider that the Son of Heaven takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother, the sun as elder brother and moon as elder sister—in rite they merit respect, hence the double-bow ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengsheng 1: relevant offices said: "The Son of Heaven fathers Heaven and mothers Earth, brothers the sun and sisters the moon—hence double bow.

sentences.zh: 謹按五嶽視三公，四瀆視諸侯，天子無拜公侯之禮，臣愚以為失尊卑之序。

translations.literal: We examine that the Five Marchmounts are treated like the Three Excellencies and the Four Watercourses like feudal lords; the Son of Heaven has no rite of bowing to dukes and marquises—we hold this reverses the order of honor and lowliness.
translations.idiomatic: Five Marchmounts equal Three Excellencies, Four Watercourses equal lords; the Son of Heaven does not bow to dukes—this reverses honor and lowliness.

sentences.zh: 其日月已下，請依舊儀。

translations.literal: The sun, moon, and below should follow former practice.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and below: former practice.

sentences.zh: 五嶽已下，署而不拜。

translations.literal: For the Five Marchmounts and below, sign but do not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Five Marchmounts and below: sign, no bow.

sentences.zh: 」制可，從之。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The edict approved and it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Approved and followed.

sentences.zh: 貞觀之禮，無祭先代帝王之文。

translations.literal: Zhenguan rites had no text on sacrificing to former dynasties' emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan rites lacked sacrifice to former emperors.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年六月，禮部尚書許敬宗等奏曰：「謹案《禮記·祭法》云：'聖王之制祀也，法施於人則祀之，以死勤事則祀之，以勞定國則祀之，能禦大災則祀之，能捍大患則祀之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Xianqing 2, Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong and others memorialized: "We have examined the Book of Rites 'Regulations of Sacrifice,' which says: 'When the sage king fixed sacrifice, those whose law extended to the people were sacrificed; those who died in diligent service; those who labored to settle the state; those who could ward off great calamity; those who could repel great peril.'
translations.idiomatic: Xianqing 2, sixth month: Xu Jingzong memorialized: "Book of Rites 'Regulations of Sacrifice' says: 'Sage kings sacrificed those whose law reached the people; who died in service; who labored to settle the state; who warded great calamity; who repelled great peril.'

sentences.zh: 」又：'堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，有功烈於人，及日月星辰，人所瞻仰；

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Furthermore: 'Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu had merit and glory among the people, as did sun, moon, and stars that people behold;
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Furthermore: 'Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu had merit among the people, as sun, moon, and stars people behold;

sentences.zh: 非此族也，不在祀典'。

translations.literal: those not of this kind are not in the canon of sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: those not of this kind are outside the sacrifice canon.'

sentences.zh: 准此，帝王合與日月同例，常加祭享，義在報功。

translations.literal: According to this, emperors should share the sun and moon's precedent and receive regular sacrifice—the meaning is repaying merit.
translations.idiomatic: By this, emperors share the sun and moon's precedent with regular sacrifice—repaying merit.

sentences.zh: 爰及隋代，並遵斯典。

translations.literal: Down to the Sui, all followed this canon.
translations.idiomatic: Through Sui all followed this canon.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖祭法無文，但以前代迄今，多行秦、漢故事。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu's sacrifice regulations had no text, but from former ages to the present Qin and Han precedents were often followed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's regulations lacked text, but Qin and Han precedents were often followed.

sentences.zh: 始皇無道，所以棄之。

translations.literal: First Emperor was without the Way and therefore abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: First Emperor was without the Way and abandoned.

sentences.zh: 漢祖典章，法垂於後。

translations.literal: Han Founder's statutes and models were law handed down to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Han Founder's models became law for later ages.

sentences.zh: 自隋已下，亦在祠例。

translations.literal: From Sui down they were also in the sacrifice precedents.
translations.idiomatic: From Sui down they were also in sacrifice precedents.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大唐稽古垂化，網羅前典，唯此一禮，咸秩未申。

translations.literal: We consider that Great Tang examines antiquity and hands down transformation, gathering former canons—only this one rite has not been fully ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Great Tang examines antiquity and gathers canons—only this rite lacks full order.

sentences.zh: 今請聿遵故事，三年一祭。

translations.literal: Now we ask to follow precedent: sacrifice once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to follow precedent: sacrifice every three years.

sentences.zh: 以仲春之月，祭唐堯於平陽，以契配；

translations.literal: In the mid-spring month sacrifice Tang Yao at Pingyang with Qi as associate;
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring: Yao at Pingyang, Qi paired;

sentences.zh: 祭虞舜於河東，以咎繇配；

translations.literal: sacrifice Yu Shun at Hedong with Gao Yao as associate;
translations.idiomatic: Shun at Hedong, Gao Yao paired;

sentences.zh: 祭夏禹于安邑，以伯益配；

translations.literal: sacrifice Yu of Xia at Anyi with Bo Yi as associate;
translations.idiomatic: Yu at Anyi, Bo Yi paired;

sentences.zh: 祭殷湯于偃師，以伊尹配；

translations.literal: sacrifice Tang of Yin at Yanshi with Yi Yin as associate;
translations.idiomatic: Tang at Yanshi, Yi Yin paired;

sentences.zh: 祭周文王於邦，以太公配；

translations.literal: sacrifice King Wen of Zhou at Bang with Grand Duke as associate;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen at Bang, Grand Duke paired;

sentences.zh: 祭武王於鎬，以周公、召公配；

translations.literal: sacrifice King Wu at Hao with Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao as associates;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu at Hao, Duke of Zhou and Shao paired;

sentences.zh: 祭漢高祖于長陵，以蕭何配。

translations.literal: sacrifice Han Gaozu at Changling with Xiao He as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu at Changling, Xiao He paired.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元二十二年正月，詔曰：「古聖帝明王、嶽瀆海鎮，用牲牢，餘並以酒脯充奠祀。

translations.literal: In the first month of Kaiyuan 22, an edict stated: "Ancient sage emperors and illustrious kings, marchmounts, watercourses, seas, and garrisons use victims of the great offering; the rest use wine and dried flesh for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 22, first month: sage emperors, marchmounts, watercourses, seas, and garrisons take great-offering victims; the rest wine and dried flesh.

sentences.zh: 」二十三年正月，詔：「自今已後，明衣絹布，並祀前五日預給。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." In the first month of the twenty-third year, an edict: "From now on, bright garments of silk and cloth shall be issued five days before sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Year 23, first month: "From now bright garments issued five days before sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」丁酉，詔：「自今已後，有大祭，宜差丞相、特進、開府、少保、少傅、尚書、御史大夫攝行事。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." On dingyou, an edict: "From now on, for great sacrifices, chancellor, special advancement, opening the government, junior guardian, junior mentor, minister, and censor-in-chief should be dispatched to perform the rite."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Dingyou: "Great sacrifices: chancellor, special advancement, opening government, junior guardian, junior mentor, minister, and censor-in-chief perform by proxy."

sentences.zh: 」天寶六載正月，詔：「三皇、五帝，於京城置令，丞。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." In the first month of Tianbao 6, an edict: "Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors shall have magistrates and assistants set up in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Tianbao 6, first month: "Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors: capital magistrates and assistants."

sentences.zh: 」七載五月，詔：「三皇已前帝王，宜於京城共置廟官。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." In the fifth month of the seventh year, an edict: "Emperors before the Three Sovereigns should jointly have temple officers set up in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Year 7, fifth month: "Pre-Three Sovereigns emperors: joint capital temple officers.

sentences.zh: 歷代帝王肇跡之處，德業可稱者，忠臣義士、孝婦烈女，所在亦置一祠宇。

translations.literal: Wherever former emperors first rose or merit was commendable, loyal ministers, righteous gentlemen, filial wives and steadfast women—each place should also set up one shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Where emperors first rose or merit shone, loyal ministers, righteous men, filial wives and steadfast women: one shrine each.

sentences.zh: 晉陽真人等並追贈，得道升仙處，度道士永修香火。

translations.literal: Jinyang Perfected Ones and the like were posthumously enfeoffed; where they attained the Way and ascended as immortals, Daoist priests were ordained to tend incense forever.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang Perfected Ones and the like were posthumously enfeoffed; immortal ascension sites received ordained priests for perpetual incense.

sentences.zh: 」九載九月，處士崔昌上《大唐五行應運曆》，以王者五十代而一千年，請國家承周、漢，以周、隋為閏。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." In the ninth month of the ninth year, Recluse Cui Chang presented the "Great Tang Five-Phase Responsive Calendar," holding that fifty generations of kings make one thousand years, and asked the state to succeed Zhou and Han with Zhou and Sui as intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Ninth year, ninth month: Recluse Cui Chang presented the "Great Tang Five-Phase Responsive Calendar," fifty generations per millennium, asking succession to Zhou and Han with Zhou and Sui intercalary.

sentences.zh: 十一月，敕：「唐承漢後，其周武王、漢高祖同置一廟並官吏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict: "Tang succeeds after Han; King Wu of Zhou and Han Gaozu shall share one temple and officers.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: Tang succeeds Han; King Wu of Zhou and Han Gaozu share one temple and officers.

sentences.zh: 」十二載九月，以魏、周、隋依舊為三王后，封韓公、介、酅公等，仍舊五廟。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." In the ninth month of the twelfth year, Wei, Zhou, and Sui remained the three former kings; Han Duke, Jie, and Xi Duke and the like were enfeoffed, still with five temples.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Twelfth year, ninth month: Wei, Zhou, and Sui as three former kings; Han, Jie, and Xi dukes enfeoffed, five temples unchanged.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載正月，詔大祭祀騂犢，量減其數。

translations.literal: In the first month of Tianbao 6, an edict: great sacrifices use reddish calves and quantities are reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 6, first month: great sacrifices use reddish calves; quantities reduced.

sentences.zh: 肅宗上元元年閏四月，改元，制以歲儉，停中小祠享祭。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of Shangyuan 1, the era was changed; an edict because the year was lean stopped middle and small sacrifice offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan 1 intercalary fourth month: era changed; lean year stopped middle and small sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 至其年仲秋，復祠文宣於太學。

translations.literal: In mid-autumn of that year, sacrifice to Literary Sage at the Imperial Academy was restored.
translations.idiomatic: That year mid-autumn: Literary Sage at Imperial Academy restored.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，春夏累月亢旱，詔大臣裴冕等十餘人，分祭川瀆以祈雨。

translations.literal: In Yongtai 2, drought lasted many months through spring and summer; an edict had ministers Pei Mian and more than ten others sacrifice separately at rivers and watercourses to pray for rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtai 2: months of spring-summer drought; Pei Mian and ten-plus ministers sacrificed at rivers and watercourses for rain.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使右常侍於休烈請依舊祠風伯、雨師於國門舊壇，復為中祠，從之。

translations.literal: Ritual Commissioner Right Regular Attendant Yu Xiulie asked to restore former sacrifice to Wind Lord and Rain Master at the old capital-gate altars as middle sacrifice; approved.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Commissioner Yu Xiulie asked Wind Lord and Rain Master restored at old gate altars as middle sacrifice; approved.

sentences.zh: 高祖武德二年，國子立周公、孔子廟。

translations.literal: In Wude 2 of Gaozu, the National University established shrines to Duke of Zhou and Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu Wude 2: National University established Duke of Zhou and Confucius shrines.

sentences.zh: 七年二月己酉，詔「諸州有明一經已上未被升擢者，本屬舉送，具以名聞，有司試策，皆加敘用。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the second month of the seventh year, an edict: "In prefectures where those who have mastered one classic or more have not been promoted, the local authority shall present them by name; the relevant offices test by policy questions and all receive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7, second month twenty-seventh: prefectures with classicists not yet promoted present by name; offices test by policy and appoint.

sentences.zh: 其吏民子弟，有識性明敏，志希學藝，亦具名申送，量共差品，並即配學。

translations.literal: Officials' and commoners' sons who are keen and aspire to learning should also be reported by name; ranks are assigned by measure and all are assigned to study.
translations.idiomatic: Keen officials' and commoners' sons: report by name, rank by measure, assign to study.

sentences.zh: 州縣及鄉，並令置學。

translations.literal: Prefectures, counties, and townships should all establish schools.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, counties, and townships: establish schools.

sentences.zh: 」丁酉，幸國子學，親臨釋奠。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." On dingyou, he visited the National University and personally performed the libation rite.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Dingyou: visited National University and performed libation in person.

sentences.zh: 引道士、沙門有學業者，與博士雜相駁難，久之乃罷。

translations.literal: They brought in Daoist priests and Buddhist monks of learning to debate mixed with the Erudites; after a long time it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Learned Daoists and monks were set to debate the Erudites until the practice was dropped.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年三月丁丑，太宗幸國子學，親觀釋奠。

translations.literal: In the third month, day dingchou, of Zhenguan 14, Taizong visited the Directorate of Studies and personally observed the libation ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 14, third month dingchou: Taizong visited the Directorate and watched the libation rites.

sentences.zh: 祭酒孔穎達講《孝經》，太宗問穎達曰：「夫子門人，曾、閔俱稱大孝，而今獨為曾說，不為閔說，何耶？

translations.literal: Libation-offering Director Kong Yingda lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; Taizong asked Yingda: "Among the Master's disciples, Zeng and Min were both styled greatly filial—why now is only Zeng expounded and not Min? Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Director Kong Yingda lectured on the Filial Classic; Taizong asked why only Zeng, not Min, was taught though both were called greatly filial.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「曾孝而全，獨為曾能達也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Zeng was filial and whole; only Zeng could reach fulfillment."
translations.idiomatic: Yingda said Zeng's filial piety was complete and he alone had fully attained it.

sentences.zh: 」制旨駁之曰：「朕聞《家語》云：曾皙使曾參鋤瓜，而誤斷其本，皙怒，援大杖以擊其背，手僕地，絕而復蘇。

translations.literal: " The imperial pronouncement rebutted: "We have heard in the Family Sayings: Zeng Xi had Zeng Shen hoe melons and he mistakenly cut the root; Xi was angry, took a great staff to strike his back, and his hand fell to the ground; he ceased breathing and then revived."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cited the Family Sayings: Zeng Xi beat Zeng Shen for cutting a melon root until the son collapsed and revived.

sentences.zh: 孔子聞之，告門人曰：'參來勿內。

translations.literal: Confucius heard it and told the disciples: "When Shen comes, do not admit him."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius told his disciples not to let Shen in.

sentences.zh: '既而曾子請焉，孔子曰：'舜之事父母也，使之，常在側；

translations.literal: ' Later Zengzi requested audience; Confucius said: 'In Shun's serving his parents, when they sent him he was always at their side;
translations.idiomatic: When Shen sought him, Confucius said Shun stayed at his parents' side when sent for;

sentences.zh: 欲殺之，乃不得。

translations.literal: when they wished to kill him he could not be reached."
translations.idiomatic: when they wished to kill him he was not there to be killed.

sentences.zh: 小棰則受，大杖則走。

translations.literal: A small staff he would accept; a great staff he would flee."
translations.idiomatic: he took a light beating but fled a heavy one.

sentences.zh: 今參于父，委身以待暴怒，陷父于不義，不孝莫大焉。

translations.literal: Now Shen before his father offered his body to await violent rage and trapped his father in unrighteousness—no filial impiety is greater."
translations.idiomatic: Shen, by submitting to his father's rage, had implicated him in wrong—the worst filial impiety.

sentences.zh: '由斯而言，孰愈于閔子騫也？

translations.literal: From this speaking, who is superior to Min Ziqian?
translations.idiomatic: Who, then, was the better son—Shen or Min Ziqian?

sentences.zh: 」穎達不能對。

translations.literal: " Yingda could not reply."
translations.idiomatic: Yingda had no answer.

sentences.zh: 太宗又謂侍臣：「諸儒各生異意，皆非聖人論孝之本旨也。

translations.literal: Taizong also told the attendant ministers: "The various Ru each produce divergent ideas—all are not the sages' basic purport in discussing filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told his ministers that scholarly disputes missed the sages' true teaching on filial piety.

sentences.zh: 孝者，善事父母，自家刑國，忠於其君，戰陳勇，朋友信，揚名顯親，此之謂孝。

translations.literal: Filial piety is doing well by parents, disciplining the family and punishing the state, being loyal to one's lord, brave in battle array, trustworthy to friends, making a name and displaying kin—this is called filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety means serving parents, ordering home and state, loyalty, battlefield courage, trust among friends, and bringing honor to one's kin.

sentences.zh: 具在經典，而論者多離其文，迥出事外，以此為教，勞而非法，何謂孝之道耶！

translations.literal: It is fully in the classics, yet those who discourse mostly depart from the text and go far outside the matter; using this as teaching is toilsome and not law—what is called the Way of filial piety!
translations.idiomatic: All this is in the classics, yet commentators stray from the text; such teaching is laborious and lawless—not filial piety at all.

sentences.zh: 」二十一年，詔曰：「左丘明、卜子夏、公羊高、谷梁赤、伏勝、高堂生、戴聖、毛萇、孔安國、劉向、鄭眾、杜子春、馬融、盧植、鄭玄、服虔、何休、王肅、王弼、杜預、范甯、賈逵總二十二座，春秋二仲，行釋奠之禮。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-first year an edict said: "Zuo Qiuming, Bu Zixia, Gongsun Gao, Guliang Chi, Fu Sheng, Gaotang Sheng, Dai Sheng, Mao Chang, Kong Anguo, Liu Xiang, Zheng Zhong, Du Zichun, Ma Rong, Lu Zhi, Zheng Xuan, Fu Qian, He Xiu, Wang Su, Wang Bi, Du Yu, Fan Ning, and Jia Kui—twenty-two seats in all—in spring and autumn at the two mid-season months perform the libation ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: Year 21: twenty-two canonical scholars were enshrined for spring and autumn libation rites at the two mid-season months.

sentences.zh: 」初，以儒官自為祭主，直雲博士姓名，昭告於先聖。

translations.literal: " At first the Ru officials themselves served as sacrifice masters, directly stating the Erudite's name and announcing to the Former Sage."
translations.idiomatic: Initially Ru officials led the rite, naming the Erudite who announced to the Former Sage.

sentences.zh: 又州縣釋奠，亦以博士為主。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county libation ceremonies also had the Erudite as master.
translations.idiomatic: County and prefectural libations likewise used Erudites as masters of ceremony.

sentences.zh: 敬宗等又奏曰：

translations.literal: Jingzong and others again memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and others memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 按《禮記·文王世子》：凡學，春官釋奠于其先師。

translations.literal: According to the "Wen Wang Shizi" chapter of the Book of Rites: In all schools, in spring the director releases the libation to his former teacher."
translations.idiomatic: They cited the Rites: each school's spring director performs libation to his former teacher.

sentences.zh: 」鄭注云：「官，謂《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《樂》之官也。

translations.literal: " Zheng's commentary says: "Director means the directors of the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu explained "director" as the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music officers.

sentences.zh: 」彼謂四時之學，將習其道，故儒官釋奠，各于其師。

translations.literal: " That refers to the four seasons' schools; when about to study the Way, therefore Ru officials perform libation each to his teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal schools libated to each instructor before studying his subject.

sentences.zh: 既非國學行體，所以不及先聖。

translations.literal: It is not the form practiced at the national academy, so it does not reach the Former Sage.
translations.idiomatic: That was not the national academy rite and did not involve the Former Sage.

sentences.zh: 至於春、秋二時合樂之日，則天子視學，命有司典秩，即總祭先聖、先師焉。

translations.literal: As for the spring and autumn days when music is combined, then the Son of Heaven inspects the school, orders the relevant offices to manage rank, and thereupon sacrifices in aggregate to the Former Sage and Former Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: At the spring and autumn combined-music days the emperor inspected the school and sacrificed together to the Former Sage and Teacher.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢釋奠，無文可檢。

translations.literal: Qin and Han libation ceremonies have no text that can be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han libation practice leaves no checkable record.

sentences.zh: 至於魏武，則使太常行事。

translations.literal: As for Cao of Wei, he had the Director of Ritual perform the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had the Director of Ritual conduct it.

sentences.zh: 自晉、宋已降，時有親行，而學官主祭，全無典實。

translations.literal: From Jin and Song downward there were times of personal performance, yet academy officers presiding over sacrifice entirely lacked canonical substance.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin and Song emperors sometimes attended, but academy officers leading sacrifice had no real precedent.

sentences.zh: 且名稱國學，樂用軒懸，樽俎威儀，蓋皆官備，在於臣下，理不合專。

translations.literal: Moreover it is called the national academy; music uses suspended bells; libation vessels and august regalia are all provided by the offices—in the hands of subordinates, by principle they should not monopolize it.
translations.idiomatic: The national academy used full court music and regalia—subordinates should not monopolize the rite.

sentences.zh: 況凡在小神，猶皆遣使行禮，釋奠既准中祀，據理必須稟命。

translations.literal: Besides, for even minor spirits envoys are still sent to perform rites; libation being classed as middle sacrifice, by principle one must receive command.
translations.idiomatic: Even minor spirits received imperial envoys; middle-grade libation required imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 今請國學釋奠，令國子祭酒為初獻，祝辭稱「皇帝謹遣」，仍令司業為亞獻，國子博士為終獻。

translations.literal: Now we request that for national-academy libation the Director of the Directorate of Studies be first offering, the prayer saying "The emperor respectfully dispatches," and still order the Vice Director as second offering and the Directorate Erudite as final offering.
translations.idiomatic: They asked the Directorate Director to make the first offering with prayer "The emperor respectfully dispatches," the Vice Director second, and the Erudite third.

sentences.zh: 其州學，刺史為初獻，上佐為亞獻，博士為終獻。

translations.literal: For prefectural schools the prefect is first offering, the senior aide second offering, and the Erudite final offering.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural schools: prefect first, senior aide second, Erudite third.

sentences.zh: 縣學，令為初獻，丞為亞獻，博士既無品秩，請主薄及尉通為終獻。

translations.literal: For county schools the magistrate is first offering, the assistant second offering; since the Erudite has no rank, we request the chief clerk and the district captain jointly as final offering.
translations.idiomatic: County schools: magistrate first, assistant second; the clerk and district captain jointly third, the Erudite having no rank.

sentences.zh: 若有闕，並以次差攝。

translations.literal: If there are vacancies, all are to be filled in order by substitution.
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies were to be filled by the next officer in order.

sentences.zh: 州縣釋奠，既請各刺史、縣令親獻主祭，望准祭社，同給明衣。

translations.literal: For prefectural and county libation, since we request each prefect and magistrate personally to offer as chief sacrificer, we hope to follow community-altar sacrifice in likewise granting bright garments.
translations.idiomatic: Local libations with prefects and magistrates presiding should grant bright garments as at community-altar rites.

sentences.zh: 修附禮令，以為永則。

translations.literal: Revise and attach to the ritual code as an eternal rule.
translations.idiomatic: The changes were to be codified permanently.

sentences.zh: 高宗顯慶二年七月，禮部尚書許敬宗等議：「依令，周公為先聖，孔子為先師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Xianqing 2 of Gaozong, Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong and others deliberated: "According to the code, the Duke of Zhou is Former Sage and Confucius is Former Teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Xianqing 2, month 7: Xu Jingzong ruled that the Duke of Zhou was Former Sage and Confucius Former Teacher.

sentences.zh: 又《禮記》云：'始立學，釋奠於先聖。

translations.literal: Also the Book of Rites says: "When first establishing a school, release libation to the Former Sage."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites required libation to the Former Sage when a school was founded.

sentences.zh: '鄭玄注云：'若周公、孔子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: 'Such as the Duke of Zhou and Confucius.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glossed this as the Duke of Zhou and Confucius.

sentences.zh: 」且周公踐極，功比帝王，請配武王。

translations.literal: " Moreover the Duke of Zhou ascended the throne and his merit matched emperors and kings; we request he be associated with King Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou had equaled emperors; they asked to pair him with King Wu.

sentences.zh: 以孔子為先聖。

translations.literal: Take Confucius as Former Sage."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius alone was to be Former Sage.

sentences.zh: 」二年，廢書、算、律學。

translations.literal: " In the second year the schools of Documents, Mathematics, and Law were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2: the Documents, Mathematics, and Law schools were abolished.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年正月，東都置國子監丞、主簿、錄事各一員，四門助教博士、四門生三百員，四門俊士二百員。

translations.literal: In the first month of Longshuo 2, at the eastern capital were established one each of Directorate vice-director, registrar, and recorder; four-gate assistant instructors and Erudites; three hundred four-gate students; and two hundred four-gate distinguished scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo 2: the eastern capital Directorate gained new officers, four-gate faculty, three hundred students, and two hundred distinguished scholars.

sentences.zh: 二月，復置律及書、算學。

translations.literal: In the second month the schools of Law and of Documents and Mathematics were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Second month: Law, Documents, and Mathematics schools were restored.

sentences.zh: 三年，以書隸蘭台，算隸秘閣局，律隸詳刑寺。

translations.literal: In the third year Documents was subordinated to the Orchid Terrace, Mathematics to the Secretariat Archive Bureau, and Law to the Detailed Punishments Office.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3: Documents went to the Orchid Terrace, Mathematics to the Archive, Law to Detailed Punishments.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年正月，高宗東封還，次鄒縣頓，祭宣父，贈太師。

translations.literal: In the first month of Qianfeng 1, Gaozong returning from the eastern feng sacrifice halted at Zou county, sacrificed to the Venerable Father, and enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfeng 1: returning from the feng, Gaozong sacrificed to Confucius at Zou and made him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 總章元年二月，皇太子弘幸國學，釋奠，贈顏回太子少師，曾參太子少保。

translations.literal: In the second month of Zongzhang 1 the crown prince Hong visited the national academy, performed libation, and enfeoffed Yan Hui as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Zeng Shen as Junior Protector to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhang 1: Crown Prince Hong libated at the academy and enfeoffed Yan Hui and Zeng Shen as heir tutors.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年五月，詔：「自今已後，《道德經》並為上經，貢舉人皆須兼通。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Yifeng 3 an edict said: "From now onward the Classic of the Way and Its Power is also a supreme classic; candidates for tribute and selection must all be versed in it."
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng 3: the Daodejing became a supreme classic required of examination candidates.

sentences.zh: 其餘經及《論語》，任依常式。

translations.literal: The remaining classics and the Analects may follow the usual forms."
translations.idiomatic: Other classics and the Analects followed the usual rules.

sentences.zh: 」則天天授三年，追封周公為褒德王，孔子為隆道公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Empress Zetian's Tianshou era the Duke of Zhou was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Commending Virtue and Confucius as Duke of Elevating the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou 3: the Duke of Zhou became King of Commending Virtue; Confucius became Duke of Elevating the Way.

sentences.zh: 則天長壽二年，自製《臣軌》兩卷，令貢舉人為業，停《老子》。

translations.literal: In Changshou 2 of Zetian she personally composed two scrolls of "Tracks for Ministers," ordering candidates for tribute and selection to take it as their study, and stopped the Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: Changshou 2: Zetian's Tracks for Ministers replaced the Laozi in the curriculum.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，停《臣軌》，復習《老子》。

translations.literal: In Shenlong 1 Tracks for Ministers was stopped and study of the Laozi resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Shenlong 1: Tracks for Ministers was dropped and the Laozi restored.

sentences.zh: 以鄒、魯百戶封隆道公，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: With a hundred households of Zou and Lu enfeoffing the Duke of Elevating the Way, posthumous title Wén Xuān.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred households in Zou and Lu supported the duke, posthumously titled Wén Xuān.

sentences.zh: 睿宗景雲二年八月丁巳，皇太子釋奠于太學。

translations.literal: On the eighth month, day dingsi, of Jingyun 2 of Ruizong the crown prince performed libation at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyun 2, eighth month dingsi: the crown prince libated at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 太極元年正月，詔：「孔宣父祠廟，令本州修飾，取側近三十戶以供灑掃。

translations.literal: In the first month of Taiji 1 an edict said: "The temple of the Venerable Father Confucius—order the native prefecture to repair it and take thirty nearby households to supply sweeping."
translations.idiomatic: Taiji 1: Confucius's temple was to be repaired and thirty households assigned to maintain it.
The edict closed.

sentences.zh: 開元七年十月戊寅，皇太子詣國學，行齒胄之禮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, day wuyin, of Kaiyuan 7 the crown prince went to the national academy and performed the cap-and-armor ceremony by age.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 7, tenth month: the crown prince performed the age-order cap ceremony at the academy.

sentences.zh: 開元十一年，春秋二時釋奠，諸州宜依舊用牲牢，其屬縣用酒脯而已。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 11, for spring and autumn libation at the two seasons, prefectures should follow the old use of ox and sheep victims; subordinate counties used only wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 11: prefectures kept full victims for libation; counties used only wine and dried meat.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，春秋二時社及釋奠，天下州縣等停牲牢，唯用酒脯，永為常式，二十四年三月，始移貢舉，遣禮部侍郎姚奕請進士帖《左傳》、《禮記》，通五及第。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year, for spring and autumn community-altar and libation at the two seasons, all prefectures and counties under Heaven stopped ox and sheep victims and used only wine and dried meat as an eternal rule; in the third month of the twenty-fourth year tribute selection was first moved, dispatching Vice Minister of Rites Yao Yi to request that jinshi candidates be examined on pasted passages from the Zuo Commentary and Book of Rites, passing five to graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 19: local libations and community rites were limited to wine and dried meat; in year 24 jinshi began posting on the Zuo Commentary and Rites, five passes to graduate.

sentences.zh: 二十五年三月，敕：「明經自今已後，貼十通五已上；

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-fifth year an edict said: "For mingjing from now on, paste ten and pass five or more;"
translations.idiomatic: Year 25: mingjing candidates had to pass five of ten pasted classics.

sentences.zh: 口問大義十條，取通六已上；

translations.literal: oral questioning on great principles ten items, take six passed or more;"
translations.idiomatic: and six of ten oral questions on great principles.

sentences.zh: 仍答時務策三道，取粗有文理者及第。

translations.literal: still answer three current-affairs policy questions, taking those with rough coherence as graduates."
translations.idiomatic: plus three policy essays of rough coherence.

sentences.zh: 進士停帖小經，宜准明經例試大經，帖十通四，然後試雜文及策，訖，封所試雜文及策，送中書、門下詳覆。

translations.literal: Jinshi stopped pasting minor classics and should follow the mingjing precedent in examining major classics, paste ten and pass four, then examine miscellaneous writings and policy; when finished, seal the examined miscellaneous writings and policy and send to the Secretariat and Chancellery for detailed review."
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi dropped minor classics, posted on major ones four of ten, then essays and policy for Secretariat review.

sentences.zh: 」二十六年正月，敕：「諸州鄉貢見訖，令引就國子監謁先師，學官為之開講，質問疑義，有司設食。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the twenty-sixth year an edict said: "When prefectural tribute presentations are concluded, order them led to the Directorate of Studies to visit the Former Teacher; academy officers open lectures for them, question doubtful meanings, and the relevant offices set out food."
translations.idiomatic: Year 26: after local tribute selections, candidates visited the Former Teacher at the Directorate for lectures and feasting.

sentences.zh: 弘文、崇文兩館學生及監內得舉人，亦聽預焉。

translations.literal: Students of the Hongwen and Chongwen institutes and those within the Directorate who had passed selection were also permitted to participate."
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen, Chongwen, and qualifying Directorate students could join.

sentences.zh: 」其日，祀先聖已下，如釋奠之禮。

translations.literal: " That day sacrifice to the Former Sage and below was like the libation ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: That day they sacrificed to the Former Sage as at libation.

sentences.zh: 青宮五品已下及朝集使，就監觀禮，遂為常式，每年行之至今。

translations.literal: Eastern-palace fifth rank and below and assembly envoys came to the Directorate to observe the rites; it then became a constant form, performed every year down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Palace and assembly envoys watched; the practice became annual.

sentences.zh: 初，開元八年，國子司業李元瓘奏稱：「先聖孔宣父廟，先師顏子配座，今其像立侍，配享合坐。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in Kaiyuan 8, Directorate Vice Director Li Yuanjin memorialized: "In the Former Sage the Venerable Father Confucius's temple, the Former Teacher Yanzi has an associated seat; now his image stands in attendance—associated enjoyment should sit."
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 8: Li Yuanjin asked seated images for Yan Hui and seated association for the Ten Wise Ones.

sentences.zh: 十哲弟子，雖復列像廟堂，不預享祀。

translations.literal: The Ten Wise disciples, though again having images arrayed in the temple hall, did not participate in enjoyment of sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Wise had images but no sacrificial share.

sentences.zh: 謹檢祠令：何休、範甯等二十二賢，猶沾從祀，望請春秋釋奠，列享在二十二賢之上。

translations.literal: We respectfully check the cult code: He Xiu, Fan Ning, and the other twenty-two worthies still partake of follow-sacrifice; we hope at spring and autumn libation to array enjoyment above the twenty-two worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two later scholars still had follow-sacrifice; the Ten Wise should rank above them.

sentences.zh: 七十子，請准舊都監堂圖形於壁，兼為立贊，庶敦勸儒風，光崇聖烈。

translations.literal: The seventy disciples—we request following the old capital Directorate hall in picturing them on the walls and also establishing eulogies, that perhaps we may encourage Ru wind and glorify the sage's majesty."
translations.idiomatic: The seventy disciples should be painted on the walls with eulogies to encourage learning.

sentences.zh: 曾參等道業可崇，獨受經于夫子，望准二十二賢預饗。

translations.literal: Zeng Shen and others have a Way and learning that can be honored; they alone received the classic from the Master—we hope to follow the twenty-two worthies in advance of enjoyment."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen and others who studied directly under the Master should join the twenty-two in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」敕改顏生等十哲為坐像，悉預從祀。

translations.literal: " An edict changed Yan Sheng and the other Ten Wise to seated images, all participating in follow-sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: An edict seated the Ten Wise and gave them follow-sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 曾參大孝，德冠同列，特為塑像，坐於十哲之次。

translations.literal: Zeng Shen's great filial piety and virtue crowned his row; specially a sculpted image was made, seated next after the Ten Wise."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen was given a special seated image after the Ten Wise for his filial piety.

sentences.zh: 圖畫七十子及二十二賢於廟壁上。

translations.literal: The seventy disciples and twenty-two worthies were painted on the temple walls.
